description: This cluster addresses LLM limitations regarding outdated or incomplete knowledge by integrating and processing external, dynamic information. Patterns focus on accessing real-time data sources, structuring raw evidence through multi-stage pipelines, and refining knowledge to improve factual accuracy, relevance, and mitigate hallucinations in LLM outputs.
These patterns describe how LLMs integrate, select, invoke, and orchestrate external tools to augment their capabilities, overcome limitations, and solve complex, multi-step tasks.

This cluster encompasses patterns focused on enhancing LLM reliability, transparency, and capabilities. It includes integrating external tools for robustness and task automation, ensuring factual accuracy and verifiability, providing explicit reasoning paths for explainability, and designing interfaces for improved human-AI interaction and data quality, all aimed at building trust and mitigating risks.
sub_patterns: Knowledge Traceability and Correctability via Explicit Reasoning Paths

description: This cluster focuses on improving AI's ability to accurately interpret diverse and often ambiguous user queries, encompassing multimodal inputs and complex natural language, to better map intent to actions and enhance user experience.

This cluster encompasses patterns where LLMs enhance their performance through iterative processes, leveraging various forms of feedback (self-generated, tool-based, automated, or user-provided) to identify errors, refine responses, and adapt plans dynamically. The core idea is continuous improvement and error recovery over multiple steps.
sub_patterns: Self-Evaluation and Termination Condition (for iterative reasoning)

description: This cluster focuses on strategies for LLMs to tackle complex, multi-step problems by breaking them into smaller sub-tasks, planning action sequences, and employing search techniques like backtracking to ensure optimal or feasible solutions under constraints.

This cluster details patterns for Large Language Models (LLMs) to learn, refine, and manage tool-use. It covers acquiring skills from demonstrations and feedback, generating training data, resolving knowledge conflicts, and enabling LLMs to create new tools, enhancing their robustness and generalizability in tool-augmented environments.
sub_patterns: Learning from Feedback (Reinforcement Learning for Tool Use)
Automated Dataset Generation for Tool-Augmented LLMs

description: This cluster encompasses patterns for optimizing RAG system performance, improving context quality and LLM robustness, and enabling efficient multi-task instruction tuning for both retrieval and generation capabilities.
sub_patterns: Knowledge Tree for RAG KV Cache
Unified Instruction Format for Multi-task LLM Training
Multi-Source Data Blending for Unified Instruction Tuning
Optimal Document Count for In-Context Learning
Unified Ranking and Generation Instruction Tuning (RankRAG)

description: This cluster encompasses advanced techniques for optimizing Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Patterns focus on improving factual consistency, reducing hallucinations, and enhancing context integration through methods like dynamic retrieval guidance, probabilistic marginalization over multiple documents, and auxiliary training tasks, enabling more robust and accurate generations.
sub_patterns: Selective Generation with Sufficient Context Signal

description: This cluster encompasses patterns focused on enhancing LLM evaluation capabilities, improving output reliability, and assessing model confidence. It includes methods for structured scoring, explicit uncertainty communication, and robust output parsing to ensure trustworthy and interpretable LLM judgments.

This cluster focuses on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and its sophisticated extensions. Patterns address LLM limitations like hallucinations and knowledge cutoffs by integrating external knowledge retrieval. It covers core RAG, iterative and adaptive retrieval for complex queries, fine-tuning for robust context utilization, and foundational retriever-reader architectures.
sub_patterns: Prompt-Tuning a Frozen LM as a Reader

description: This cluster focuses on methods to enhance, control, and evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) behavior. It includes advanced prompting strategies for better output quality and ethical alignment, rigorous evaluation frameworks (often LLM-based) for truthfulness and performance, and techniques to ensure data consistency and mitigate biases.

This cluster encompasses techniques designed to improve Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to perform complex, multi-step reasoning by explicitly guiding them to generate intermediate thought processes. It includes foundational Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, its zero-shot and few-shot variations, and advanced methods for automated exemplar creation, consistency, context handling, and multilingual application. The primary goal is to boost accuracy, transparency, and robustness in logical, mathematical, and complex question-answering tasks.

This cluster details patterns for integrating Large Language Models with Knowledge Graphs to achieve faithful, interpretable, and accurate reasoning. It covers methods for LLMs to plan, retrieve, and reason over KG paths, extract entities, and iteratively guide KG exploration, often leveraging specific prompt engineering or instruction tuning to overcome LLM limitations and utilize structured knowledge effectively.
sub_patterns: Iterative Prompting for Guided KG Exploration and Reasoning

description: This cluster focuses on improving LLM performance on complex reasoning tasks by prompting them to first generate a structured plan and then execute it step-by-step. It emphasizes task decomposition and a methodical approach to problem-solving.

This cluster encompasses patterns where Large Language Models (LLMs) interact dynamically with Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to perform deep, verifiable reasoning. LLMs act as agents to explore, query, and leverage structured knowledge from KGs, mitigating hallucinations and enhancing accuracy for complex, knowledge-intensive tasks like Question Answering. Patterns include various integration strategies, from retrieval augmentation to tight-coupling and iterative exploration frameworks, often with efficiency considerations.
sub_patterns: Semantic Parsing for Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA)
LLM-Guided Beam Search for KG Exploration

description: These patterns extend linear reasoning by modeling problem-solving as a tree or graph of 'thoughts'. They enable exploring multiple reasoning paths, evaluating intermediate steps, and handling complex dependencies for robust solutions.
sub_patterns: Tree of Thoughts (ToT) / Graph of Thoughts (GoT)

description: This cluster focuses on strategies that improve LLM performance on complex reasoning tasks by explicitly breaking them down into smaller, more manageable subproblems or sequential steps. Patterns often involve solving these subtasks individually, sometimes leveraging external tools or information retrieval, to build towards a final solution.

Agents iteratively interleave reasoning (Thought), actions (Action) with tools/environment, and observation processing. This enables dynamic interaction, adaptive behavior, and self-correction in complex tasks.

This cluster focuses on enhancing LLM reasoning accuracy and reliability. Patterns involve generating multiple diverse reasoning paths or answers, employing various verification and scoring mechanisms, and then selecting or refining the optimal solution through self-correction, external validation, or ensemble methods.

This cluster focuses on advanced techniques to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) capabilities in complex reasoning, instruction following, and domain-specific adaptation. It includes various finetuning methods (Instruction, CoT, Domain-Specific) and sophisticated prompting strategies (CoT, Active, Complexity-based, AutoCoT), often employing multi-model frameworks or planning for improved faithfulness and robustness.
sub_patterns: Two-LLM Framework for Reasoning Step Selection and Generation

description: This cluster leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) and generative AI to overcome limitations in data availability, knowledge utilization, and personalized content creation. Patterns involve integrating retrieval and reasoning, generating synthetic data for training, and creating highly customized content based on user intent and feedback.

This cluster focuses on building advanced AI agents by integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with modular components like memory, tools, and planning. These architectures enhance LLM capabilities, enable autonomous multi-step task execution, manage context, and interact with environments, promoting flexibility and reusability.
sub_patterns: Modular Reasoning, Knowledge and Language (MRKL) System

description: This cluster encompasses a range of methods and tools focused on making machine learning models, particularly black-boxes, transparent and understandable. It includes techniques for local (instance-specific) and global (overall model) interpretability, feature importance analysis, identifying biases in data subgroups, and interactive exploration to enhance trust, debug models, and provide actionable insights.
sub_patterns: DivExplorer Interactive System (Interactive Divergent Subgroup Exploration)

description: This cluster focuses on patterns that enhance Large Language Models by addressing their memory limitations, enabling dynamic knowledge updates, and improving efficiency and adaptability. Key themes include managing various memory types (parametric, non-parametric, short-term, long-term), extending context handling, and optimizing fine-tuning and query processing.
sub_patterns: Automatic Classifier Training Data Generation (for Query Complexity)
Memory Management (Working Memory / Short-Term Memory / Long-Term Memory)

description: Patterns in this cluster enhance LLM performance by integrating external, up-to-date knowledge. They mitigate hallucinations and limited domain knowledge by retrieving relevant information from external sources and augmenting the LLM's input, leading to more accurate, factual, and contextually rich responses for knowledge-intensive tasks.

This cluster encompasses patterns designed to optimize the efficiency, speed, and accuracy of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It includes strategies for RAGSequence decoding (balancing speed vs. thoroughness) and advanced caching mechanisms for LLM intermediate states (Key-Value tensors) to reduce computation, improve throughput, and manage memory.
sub_patterns: Multilevel Dynamic Knowledge Caching for RAG (RAGCache)

description: These patterns focus on overcoming LLM knowledge limitations by integrating them with external, dynamic, and up-to-date information sources like the web, databases, or vector stores. This enhances factual accuracy, reduces hallucinations, and enables real-time information access.
sub_patterns: Live Web Access with Controlled Interaction

description: This cluster encompasses patterns designed to optimize the Key-Value (KV) cache in Large Language Model (LLM) serving systems. Strategies include reusing cached tensors for shared prefixes, efficient memory management via paging, minimizing data transfer between memory tiers, and enhancing fault tolerance for critical cache components.
sub_patterns: Replication of Critical KV Cache Nodes

description: This cluster focuses on how AI models, particularly Foundation Models, extend their capabilities by interacting with, understanding, creating, and orchestrating external tools. It covers methods for models to comprehend tool functionalities via prompting, autonomously generate new tools, compose existing tools in novel ways, and collaborate with other AI agents for complex problem-solving. The overarching goal is to enable AI to tackle real-world, domain-specific tasks more effectively and efficiently.

This cluster encompasses patterns that enable AI agents to generate effective, coherent, and realistic multi-step plans. It covers strategies for both static and dynamic planning, incorporating real-world knowledge and constraints, managing long-term complexity, and ensuring alignment between internal reasoning and external actions.

This cluster describes advanced methods for AI models to learn and adapt tool use. It includes learning optimal strategies (meta-learning), personalizing interactions for users, and progressive mastery of complex tools, aiming for enhanced adaptability and efficiency.

This cluster focuses on enhancing foundation models for code generation by integrating external tools (e.g., API search, testing environments). This allows models to dynamically consult resources, improving accuracy, context-specificity, and handling complex, real-world software engineering tasks interactively.

This cluster focuses on augmenting LLM reasoning capabilities by integrating external computational tools or formalisms. It addresses the limitations of natural language for complex, precise, or structured tasks by creating synergistic loops or incorporating structured frameworks to improve performance and control.

This cluster focuses on optimizing the execution of multiple tools or subtasks within complex workflows. It addresses both the sequential management of inter-tool dependencies and the parallel execution of independent subtasks to enhance efficiency and task completion.

This cluster focuses on patterns that enable AI agents to learn, adapt, and self-correct in complex, dynamic, and open-world environments. Key mechanisms include introspection, feedback loops, internal world models for simulation-based planning, and structured approaches to skill acquisition and goal decomposition, often leveraging memory and iterative refinement.

This cluster focuses on patterns for guiding LLMs to generate responses in specific, machine-readable formats (e.g., JSON, XML, CSV) rather than free-form text. This facilitates automated parsing, integration with other systems, and consistent data extraction.

These patterns enhance LLM capabilities for complex mathematical, programming, and logical tasks by integrating code generation and execution. They interleave natural language reasoning with program-based tool use, leveraging interpreters or custom plugins for precise computation and dynamic problem-solving.

This cluster focuses on methods for training LLMs to effectively use tools and perform complex, interactive tasks. It emphasizes overcoming data scarcity through synthetic data generation (e.g., using powerful LLMs or simulators) and structured data curation, followed by imitation or staged policy learning to enable robust agentic behaviors.
sub_patterns: Staged Policy Learning for Agentic LLMs
Few-Shot Prompting for Structured Trajectory Generation

description: This cluster focuses on augmenting LLMs with external code execution capabilities to achieve precise numerical computation, symbolic manipulation, and complex algorithmic execution, overcoming the inherent limitations of natural language reasoning.

This cluster focuses on patterns where an AI agent iteratively corrects its errors and refines its approach based on feedback, especially from external tools, to achieve robustness and accuracy in complex, multi-step tasks.

This cluster encompasses patterns for building, optimizing, and training Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. It covers dense semantic retrieval, efficient knowledge base indexing, leveraging pretrained generative models, and advanced training strategies for scalability and domain adaptation in knowledge-intensive NLP tasks.
sub_patterns: Open-Book Question Answering with InContext RALM
Control Token for Multi-task Generative Models
End-to-End Retriever Training (for RAG Domain Adaptation)

description: This cluster describes patterns for enhancing and optimizing InContext Retrieval-Augmented Language Models (RALM). It includes methods for dynamically deciding when to retrieve knowledge and sophisticated techniques for reranking and selecting the most relevant documents to improve LM performance, accuracy, and efficiency, often without modifying the LM itself.

This cluster encompasses patterns for enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) by integrating them with external tools. It covers strategies for leveraging specialized tools, managing the context window for effective tool interaction, and enabling LLMs to learn and orchestrate tool use efficiently to overcome limitations like hallucination and lack of real-time data.

This cluster encompasses various techniques for designing and optimizing prompts to guide Generative AI models. It includes methods for providing examples (FewShot, SGICL), defining roles or styles (Role, Style Prompting), automating prompt optimization (APE), and the fundamental instruction-only approach (ZeroShot).

This cluster encompasses advanced prompt engineering techniques aimed at enhancing LLM performance, particularly in reasoning, query comprehension, and few-shot learning through strategic exemplar selection and arrangement.

This cluster focuses on techniques for generating, optimizing, and structuring prompts to enhance LLM performance. It includes methods for automated prompt creation, discovery of optimal prompt formats, selection of best templates, and chaining prompts for complex, multi-step problem-solving.

This cluster comprises patterns that enhance LLM performance on complex tasks through structured, multi-step interactions. Techniques involve decomposing problems, refining inputs, or recursively processing subproblems to improve speed, accuracy, and reasoning by managing context and irrelevant information.

This cluster focuses on advanced Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting techniques designed to enhance reasoning accuracy, structure, and robustness. Patterns include methods for handling uncertainty in reasoning paths, explicitly guiding the LLM away from incorrect reasoning, consolidating multiple reasoning attempts, and structuring CoT outputs for clarity.

This cluster encompasses patterns designed to mitigate biases, enhance fairness, and improve the overall quality, robustness, and cultural relevance of LLM outputs. Techniques include balanced data selection, attribute variation, and critical evidence aggregation.

This cluster focuses on advanced techniques for optimizing prompt construction and in-context learning (ICL) demonstrations. Patterns address challenges like generating diverse prompts, handling ambiguous inputs, and aligning examples for multilingual tasks to enhance model performance and robustness.

This cluster focuses on advanced techniques to optimize interactions with Large Language Models. It includes methods for automated prompt improvement through iterative refinement or gradient-free search, as well as strategies for enhancing computational efficiency and reducing costs by batching multiple inputs or candidates into single LLM calls for evaluation or pruning tasks.

This cluster encompasses prompting strategies designed to enhance machine translation quality and accuracy. Techniques include iterative refinement, leveraging external linguistic resources, task decomposition, cross-lingual transfer, and human-in-the-loop interaction to address challenges like ambiguity, long texts, and low-resource languages.
sub_patterns: PARC Prompts Augmented by Retrieval Cross-lingually

description: This cluster focuses on methods to boost the cross-lingual cognitive capabilities of multilingual LLMs. It involves leveraging both source and target languages for in-context examples to improve performance on cross-lingual tasks.

This cluster encompasses advanced prompting techniques primarily focused on controlling and guiding AI models for generating, manipulating, or understanding multimodal content, such as images and 3D objects. Patterns involve using various prompt formats (text, image, 3D) to achieve specific creative outcomes, apply transformations, or prevent undesired elements.

This cluster comprises patterns that extend established text-based reasoning techniques (like Chain-of-Thought, Graph-of-Thought, and Least-to-Most) to the multimodal domain. They enable complex problem-solving by integrating visual context and generating intermediate steps or representations (e.g., thought graphs, images, sub-questions) across different modalities.

This cluster focuses on enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to act as intelligent agents, interacting with external environments and tools. Patterns address structuring LLM inputs (state), outputs (actions/code), and decision-making (policy) to facilitate deterministic and effective task execution beyond free-form text generation.
sub_patterns: Structured Action Space for Agentic LLM

description: Enhances LLM evaluation by assigning distinct roles or personas to AI agents. Often uses a multi-agent debate framework to generate diverse perspectives and achieve more robust and nuanced assessments.

This cluster focuses on designing flexible and cost-effective frameworks for integrating LLMs with Knowledge Graphs. Patterns address computational expense, rigid architectures, and problematic entity information by emphasizing modularity, abstraction, and strategic LLM interaction to enhance efficiency, adaptability, and robustness.

This cluster focuses on patterns for enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to reliably and accurately interact with external APIs and tools. It encompasses structured API documentation, synthetic data generation, retriever-aware finetuning, constraint-aware API selection, robust evaluation of generated API calls, and fallback mechanisms for external knowledge limitations.
sub_patterns: AST-based Hallucination Detection for Code Generation
Structured API Documentation for LLM Consumption

description: This cluster details how Large Language Models (LLMs) are leveraged across various aspects of recommender systems. It covers their use for direct recommendation, conversational interaction, deep content interpretation, knowledge graph enrichment, automating ML selection, and generating transparent explanations.
sub_patterns: LLMs for Direct Recommendation (In-context Learning & CoT)

description: This cluster encompasses advanced techniques for training and optimizing large language models, especially for complex, multi-step agentic tasks. It leverages human feedback (demonstrations and preferences) for initial skill acquisition, alignment with human values, and efficient reinforcement learning, often combining methods like Behavior Cloning, Reward Modeling, and inference-time selection.
sub_patterns: Human Feedback for Quality Optimization (Reward Modeling & RLHF)
Dual Data Collection for Agentic LLM Training
Behavior Cloning for Initial Skill Acquisition
